1.why: Three options close a parenthesis, so a parenthesis must be open; between ')' and '),' the bare close is the unmarked choice.

2.why: Dangling-modifier set: only B supplies a human agent ('conservators found') that could perform an opening participle.

3.why: Two options keep the preposition 'in'; the comma version is the one that can close a supplementary element.

4.why: Singular present-perfect 'has dropped' is the standard key against a plural, a future-perfect and a past-progressive distractor.

5.why: Infinitive/gerund/noun/finite-clause family; the infinitive is the only form that works after a purpose or 'agreed/decided' verb.

6.why: Stem shows a singular appositive 'a sprawling epic', so singular 'work,' with a comma.

7.why: Comma is the only mark that fits a supplementary or coordinating continuation without demanding an independent clause or a list.

8.why: 'By the time ... signed' forces the past perfect 'had fought'.

9.why: Only C makes 'the mural' the subject, which the withheld opening modifier most plausibly describes.

10.why: Colon correctly introducing a noun-phrase list; A gives a clause after the colon, C says 'such as:' and D mismatches dash with semicolon.

11.why: Nonrestrictive relative 'which' against a comma-splice pronoun, a coordinated clause and restrictive 'that'.

12.why: Semicolon is the only option joining two independent clauses ('...clarity' / 'astronomers...').

13.why: Colon before the list 'flour...' is the only clean introduction; the others are a fused clause, a mispunctuated 'and', or a bad inversion.

14.why: Subject-case 'she' against object, possessive and reflexive distractors — the classic compound-subject key.

15.why: Singular present 'is' against a plural, a simple past and a present perfect.

16.why: Same four forms as 15 reshuffled, so the key is likely the plural 'were' this time.

17.why: Plural present 'are' — two singular and one plural-perfect distractor bracket it.

18.why: Counterfactual conditional wants 'would have been damped'; passive plus perfect is the only fully-marked form.

19.why: Past perfect 'had lain' — intransitive 'lie' with a prior-to-past reference.

20.why: Infinitive/gerund/participle/finite family; 'to listen' is the parallel infinitive.

21.why: Same infinitive family; 'to collaborate' parallels a preceding infinitive against gerund, clause and nominalization.

22.why: Dangling-modifier set like item 2: only A names a concrete agent ('the research team') for the withheld participial opener.

23.why: Stem's delayed subject 'several complaints' is plural, so 'were'.

24.why: Third repeat of the infinitive family; 'to present' is the parallel form.
